items.text: what to prove instead of what to learn
items.reason: The document explicitly says the information goal should describe what you want to learn, not what you want to prove.

items.text: target not specific enough to guide 45-90 minutes
items.reason: The charter checklist requires the target to be specific enough to guide exploration and coverable in 45-90 minutes.

items.text: summary after the fact instead of during session
items.reason: The document insists on real-time notes during the session and lists relying on memory afterward as an anti-pattern.

items.text: names at least four of the seven HICCUPS oracles
items.evidence: | **H** | History | Does current behavior match past behavior? | Did this work in the last release? Has the behavior changed subtly? |
items.reason: The HICCUPS table names all seven oracles: History, Image, Comparable, Claims, User expectations, Product, Standards.

items.text: missing the oracle lens concept
items.reason: The document defines an oracle as a principle for recognizing problems and frames heuristics as lenses.

items.text: treats HICCUPS as a checklist to complete exhaustively
items.reason: The document explicitly states heuristics are not checklists to exhaustively complete.

items.text: no connection to actual bugs found
items.reason: Findings are tied to actual bugs, e.g. BUG-456 traced from session log to regression test.

items.text: no edge cases at zero or maximum
items.reason: Boundary heuristics include zero, maximum, max+1, empty collection, and max length.

items.text: vague boundaries instead of specific values
items.reason: Boundaries are given as specific values such as 0, 1, 1000, 100000 records and page-size 20/21 items.

items.text: no reflection on what was unexpected
items.reason: The debrief template asks 'What surprised you?' and 'What was harder than expected?'.

items.text: no mention of varying conditions
items.reason: The 'when you find something interesting' loop instructs to vary the conditions across data, users, browsers.

items.text: session longer than 90 minutes
items.reason: The document time-boxes sessions to 45-90 minutes and lists 3-hour sessions as an anti-pattern.

items.text: no test reference to the original bug
items.reason: The example test name and comment reference the original BUG-456.

items.text: no assertion on the validation error
items.reason: The Playwright example asserts the 'Email is required' validation error is visible.

items.text: does not verify that invalid state is prevented
items.reason: The example asserts the page does not navigate to the confirmation URL, verifying the invalid state is prevented.

items.text: no mention of first-time user perspective
items.reason: The Familiarity lens and the 'never used this product before' what-if scenario cover the first-time user perspective.

items.text: missing at least 2 of the 3 F-E-W lenses
items.reason: All three F-E-W lenses (Familiarity, Explainability, World) are present.

items.text: no connection to how real users in different regions behave
items.reason: The World lens and what-if bank address different locales, time zones, RTL text, and number formats.

items.text: does not address state transition scenarios from the heuristic
items.reason: The document provides a full state transition heuristics bank and references it for regression charters.

items.text: assumes the fix is complete without testing edge cases
items.reason: The document requires verifying the test fails on the buggy build and passes on the fix, and varying conditions for findings.

items.text: treats exploration as less rigorous than automation
items.reason: The document lists treating exploration as 'not real testing' as an anti-pattern and asserts equal rigor.

items.text: suggests automating first before exploration
items.reason: The document positions exploration as the source of findings that then feed automation, not the reverse.

items.text: no pipeline from finding to regression test
items.reason: An explicit exploration-to-automation pipeline with conversion steps and a worked example is provided.
